coverage: 120 seeded randomized configurations: output, load, battery capacity and initial state, transmission, work rate, deadline and entry duration.
35 independent midpoint numerical integration oracles, using 0.07 simulated-second samples and a stated conservative discretization error bound.
Power-energy units, stored-energy conservation including curtailment and unserved load, zero/capacity bounds, and actual versus fixed-output warning forecast.
50 mixed-control histories with timestamp-equivalent holds, resumes and speed changes, compared across randomized frame partitions.
Zero-duration recall at the expired deadline consistently classified late; terminal state cannot be revived; minimum-reserve plan remains executable.
Artificial microsecond increments preserve work both near zero and after a whole-section boundary.
Default positive-duration entry may finish exactly at the deadline.
limitations: Checks an authored mathematical model; does not validate physical hardware, clinical dosimetry, learning outcomes, live space weather or rendering.
Randomized coverage is reproducible but finite; numerical oracle tolerances account for independent discrete integration and battery clipping.
Historical radiation measurements are documented separately in docs/SCIENCE-JOURNEY-SOURCES.md; this audit checks their implementation units, not a new primary-source measurement.
